title: This Deadly Heat Wave Has a Culprit
author: Emma Burretta
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/Screenshot-2026-07-09-at-4.01.05-PM-680x528.png)

Photo by [Akanda
Kilicarslan](https://unsplash.com/@akroxas?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

Temperatures have soared globally this summer. And far from simply being
uncomfortable, it’s killing people.

This past July 4th was [one of the hottest in U.S.
history](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/the-growing-dangers-of-record-heat-
waves-like-the-one-engulfing-july-4th-celebrations). While Americans gathered
to celebrate the country’s 250th birthday, [dozens died from extreme
heat](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/05/heatwave-deaths-weather)
— and the toll may still rise. In Europe, which has seen its own devastating
heat wave, some [3,700 people have died](https://www.dw.com/en/heat-wave-
european-countries-report-3700-excess-deaths/a-77823303). And the heat has
become so extreme in Pakistan that people’s teeth are literally [dissolving in
their mouths.
](https://www.earthisland.org/journal/index.php/magazine/entry/Extreme-heat-
is-rapidly-decaying-teeth-in-pakistan/#%23)

This is only the beginning of extreme heat this summer — and if we don’t stop
the climate crisis, for the rest of time. Scientists are warning that this
marks [“uncharted territory” in rising
temperatures.](https://www.nbcnews.com/science/climate-change/ocean-
temperatures-hit-record-high-in-june-rcna352514)

The good news? We know the solution. To build a better world, with cheaper and
cleaner energy, we have to phase out fossil fuels and transition to green
energy. This process is easier and cheaper than ever. Some [90 percent of
renewable energy is now cheaper than fossil
fuels](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/around-90-renewables-cheaper-
than-fossil-fuels-worldwide-irena-says-2025-07-22/), and renewables don’t heat
our planet [the way that fossil fuels do](https://science.nasa.gov/climate-
change/causes/).

The bad news? Fossil fuel companies, and the politicians who support them, are
trying to block this transition. Companies like Exxon have known [for over 50
years](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/exxon-knew-about-climate-
change-almost-40-years-ago/) that fossil fuels cause climate change — and that
rising temperatures would cost lives. But they’ve tried to bury this
information, stall the transition, and [deceive the
public](https://climateintegrity.org/news/view/new-report-big-oils-deceptive-
climate-ads) that fossil fuels aren’t responsible.

I’ve seen this play out firsthand.

When I was 17, I spent a sunny week in Dubai at the 28th United Nations annual
climate conference (COP28). I was so excited to attend the conference. I met
other activists passionate about renewable energy and taking down the fossil
fuel industry. I even attended lobbying meetings with the lead U.S.
negotiators, Trigg Talley and Sue Biniaz.

Everything in Dubai felt larger than life — from the Burj Khalifa to the
massive dome in the middle of the conference center. But over the week, the
conference began to feel more and more dystopian. The fossil fuel industry had
[sent 2,456 lobbyists to that
COP](https://kickbigpollutersout.org/articles/release-record-number-fossil-
fuel-lobbyists-attend-cop28) — and despite the loud cries of activists and
scientists, their voices drowned ours out.

At the end of the conference, we had a small win — fossil fuels were mentioned
in a COP text for the first time ever. But the language was so weak that the
statement felt almost meaningless. The text did nothing to change the
trajectory of the climate crisis.

The fossil fuel industry has propagated lies about climate change for years.
They’ve tried to convince us that climate change is our fault instead of
theirs, with campaigns around “carbon footprints” — [a concept created by
BP](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2021/aug/23/big-oil-coined-
carbon-footprints-to-blame-us-for-their-greed-keep-them-on-the-hook) — and
recycling, [which was popularized by the plastics
industry](https://www.npr.org/2024/02/15/1231690415/plastic-recycling-waste-
oil-fossil-fuels-climate-change) but has never managed to efficiently recycle
plastics themselves.

They have also [spent hundreds of millions of
dollars](https://insideclimatenews.org/news/08092025/energy-sector-lobbying-
spending/) on influencing climate decision making spaces — from United Nations
conferences to Washington, D.C. Big Oil spent [$445 million during the 2024
elections](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/jan/23/big-oil-445m-trump-
congress) — and in return has gotten [$40 billion in fossil fuel
subsidies](https://e360.yale.edu/digest/republican-spending-bill-fossil-fuel-
subsidies) from the Trump administration.

The time has come for us to rise up against this deceptive and powerful
industry, to finally kick them out of spaces with influence. It is high time
for us to stop being manipulated by fossil fuel companies that are only out to
make a profit and harm us.

As temperatures rise, we are now in a battle of people vs. fossil fuels. We
must win — it’s a matter of life and death.
